'''Super Male Vitality''' is a dietary supplement that is part of a line of products promoted by radio host and conspiracy theorist Alex Jones, through his media platform, Infowars. The product has been marketed as a testosterone booster that purportedly enhances male vitality and overall physical performance.

=== Product launch covered by Knowledge Fight===
[[42: March 11, 2014|Episode 42]] of '''Knowledge Fight''' covers  Alex introducing Super Male Vitality. Dan and Jordan discuss the chiropractor, Dr. Edward F. Group, DC who created the product, Rob Dew's troubling description of the effects in the bedroom, and conclude with Alex pouring the liquid on a burger before carelessly eating it while going to calls.

===Conspiracies and Marketing Tactics===

Launched in the early 2010s, Super Male Vitality has been marketed using aggressive advertising strategies that often accompany conspiratorial themes, particularly those propagated by Infowars. Promotional materials frequently suggest that the product can counteract alleged efforts by various governments and global entities to undermine public health and masculinity, themes commonly echoed in Jones's broadcasts.

===Controversies===

Super Male Vitality has faced significant scrutiny and skepticism from medical experts and consumer advocacy groups, who challenge its efficacy and the science behind its claims. Numerous analyses have pointed to the lack of credible scientific evidence supporting the product's purported health benefits, with critics arguing that the marketing exploits fear and misinformation.

The product has also been associated with broader controversies surrounding Infowars and Alex Jones, including misleading or exaggerated health claims and the dissemination of conspiracy theories. In some instances, regulatory bodies have scrutinized the advertising practices associated with such supplements, highlighting concerns over consumer deception and the promotion of pseudoscience.
